alerts.title: Carbamazepine contraindicated with DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines list carbamazepine as a contraindication for DTG, and note that carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70%, recommending use of valproic acid instead. The patient was started on carbamazepine 2 weeks ago while already on DTG. The viral load has risen from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence, consistent with reduced DTG exposure. The patient is already on sodium valproate, which the guidelines specifically recommend as the alternative antiepileptic.

evidence.recommended_action: Stop carbamazepine and manage seizures with valproic acid as guidelines recommend. Repeat viral load after adjustment and assess for resistance if viremia persists.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with elevated level
alerts.message: The patient has a carbamazepine level of 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4–12), with symptoms of ataxia, nystagmus, tremor, dizziness, and headache. Hyponatraemia (Na 128 mmol/L) is also consistent with carbamazepine toxicity. The clinician plans to reduce the dose and repeat the level. However, given the DTG interaction and guideline contraindication, discontinuation rather than dose reduction is warranted. ALT 68 U/L may also reflect carbamazepine hepatotoxicity, though valproate is another potential cause.

evidence.recommended_action: Discontinue carbamazepine entirely rather than dose-reducing, given the DTG contraindication. Monitor sodium and ALT until normal. Use valproate for seizure management.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load requires adherence support
alerts.message: Guidelines state that virological monitoring detects treatment failure early and indicates need to switch therapy to reduce resistance accumulation. The viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL within 6 months. While the DTG–carbamazepine interaction is the likely cause of reduced DTG levels, the plan does not address adherence counselling or a repeat viral load after correcting the interaction. Early repeat VL testing is needed to confirm whether viremia resolves once DTG levels are restored.

evidence.recommended_action: After stopping carbamazepine, repeat viral load in 2–3 months. Provide enhanced adherence support. If still detectable, proceed to genotype testing per guidelines.
